# 1 Samuel Chapter 25 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 164-165 | **Source Images:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1SA_025_page_001.jpg, 1SA_025_page_002.jpg, 1SA_025_page_003.jpg

---

**1** And Samuel died. And all Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. And David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

**2** Now there was a man in Maon, and his business was in Carmel. And the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. And he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

**3** And the name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. And the woman was of good understanding and beautiful in appearance. But the man was harsh and evil in his deeds, and he was a Calebite.

**4** And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

**5** And David sent ten young men. And David said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel and go to Nabal and greet him in my name.

**6** And thus you shall say to him who lives in prosperity: 'Peace be to you, and peace be to your house, and peace be to all that you have.

**7** Now I have heard that you have shearers. Now the shepherds who belong to you were with us, and we did not harm them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the days they were in Carmel.

**8** Ask your young men and they will tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a feast day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son David.'"

**9** And the young men of David came and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in the name of David. And they waited.

**10** And Nabal answered the servants of David and said, "Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? Today there are many servants who are breaking away, each from his master.

**11** Shall I then take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men whom I do not know where they come from?"

**12** And the young men of David turned on their way and went back. And they came and told him according to all these words.

**13** And David said to his men, "Each man strap on his sword." And each man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. And about four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred remained with the baggage.

**14** And one of the young men told Abigail, the wife of Nabal, saying, "Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he railed at them.

**15** But the men were very good to us, and we were not harmed, and we did not miss anything all the days we went about with them while we were in the field.

**16** They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the time we were with them tending the sheep.

**17** Now therefore know and consider what you will do, for evil is determined against our master and against all his house. And he is such a worthless man that one cannot speak to him."

**18** And Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread and two skins of wine and five prepared sheep and five seahs of roasted grain and one hundred clusters of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs. And she loaded them on the donkeys.

**19** And she said to her young men, "Go on before me; behold, I am coming after you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

**20** And it came to pass as she was riding on the donkey and coming down under the cover of the mountain, that behold, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.

**21** Now David had said, "Surely in vain I have guarded all that this fellow has in the wilderness, and nothing was missing of all that belongs to him. And he has returned me evil for good.

**22** Thus may God do to the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave of all who belong to him by the morning light so much as one who urinates against a wall."

**23** And when Abigail saw David, she hurried and dismounted from the donkey and fell before David on her face and bowed to the ground.

**24** And she fell at his feet and said, "On me alone, my lord, be the guilt. And please let your maidservant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your maidservant.

**25** Let not my lord, I pray, set his heart on this worthless man, on Nabal, for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your maidservant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.

**26** And now, my lord — as the LORD lives and as your soul lives — since the LORD has withheld you from coming into bloodguilt and from saving yourself by your own hand, now let your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord be as Nabal.

**27** And now, this blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord — let it be given to the young men who follow at the feet of my lord.

**28** Please forgive the transgression of your maidservant. For the LORD will surely make for my lord a sure house, because my lord is fighting the battles of the LORD, and evil shall not be found in you all your days.

**29** And should a man rise up to pursue you and to seek your soul, the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God. But the souls of your enemies — he shall sling them out as from the hollow of a sling.

**30** And it shall come to pass, when the LORD has done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you prince over Israel,

**31** that this shall not be to you a stumbling block or an offense of heart to my lord — that you have shed blood without cause and that my lord has saved himself. And when the LORD has done good to my lord, then remember your maidservant."

**32** And David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.

**33** And blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from saving myself by my own hand.

**34** For indeed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from harming you — if you had not hurried and come to meet me, surely there would not have been left to Nabal by the morning light so much as one who urinates against a wall."

**35** And David received from her hand what she had brought to him. And he said to her, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and have accepted your person."

**36** And Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he was holding a feast in his house, like the feast of a king. And the heart of Nabal was merry within him, for he was very drunk. So she told him nothing, small or great, until the morning light.

**37** And it came to pass in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, that his wife told him these things. And his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.

**38** And it came to pass, about ten days later, that the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

**39** And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal and has kept his servant from evil. And the LORD has returned the evil of Nabal on his own head." And David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her as his wife.

**40** And the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel and spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you, to take you as his wife."

**41** And she arose and bowed with her face to the ground, and she said, "Behold, your maidservant is a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord."

**42** And Abigail hurried and arose and rode on a donkey, with five of her young women attending her. And she went after the messengers of David and became his wife.

**43** And David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel. And both of them became his wives.

**44** Now Saul had given Michal his daughter, the wife of David, to Palti the son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

Chapter 25 is the longest chapter in the David narrative, presenting a carefully structured account: Nabal's folly, Abigail's wisdom, and divine resolution. Samuel's death is noted tersely in verse 1, forming a hinge between the prophetic era and the era of David's rise.

In verse 3, Nabal is described as a כָּלִבִּי (Calibbi, "Calebite") — a descendant of Caleb, not a pejorative. His name נָבָל means "fool" or "senseless," a wordplay Abigail herself exploits in verse 25: כִּנְבָל שְׁמוֹ כֵּן־הוּא ("as his name is, so is he").

Verse 22 contains the idiomatic expression מַשְׁתִּין בְּקִיר (mashtin beqir, "one who urinates against a wall"), a crude designation for males — preserved here in literal translation per formal equivalence principles. Verse 29 contains the theologically rich phrase צְרוּרָה בִּצְרוֹר הַחַיִּים (tserurah bitseror hachayyim, "bound in the bundle of the living"), rendered with the convention of "soul" for נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh). This phrase became a central Jewish memorial formula (צ.ב.ל.ה).

Abigail's speech (vv. 24-31) is one of the most rhetorically sophisticated in the Hebrew Bible, weaving together legal language, prophetic anticipation, and diplomatic skill. Her reference to a "sure house" (בַּיִת נֶאֱמָן, bayit ne'eman) in verse 28 anticipates the Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7.

— LOGOS (Λόγος), translated from the Leningrad Codex (B19A)
